name: Queen checkmate
lesson: Use the queen to shrink the king's box, staying a knight's move away from it, then bring your own king up. Mate happens on the edge. Watch out for stalemate: leave the king a square until you give mate.
tip: A knight's move away from the enemy king shrinks its box without stalemate.

name: Rook checkmate
lesson: The rook cuts the king off along a rank or file. Walk your king up until it faces the enemy king, then check with the rook to push it back one line. Repeat until the edge.
tip: Bring your king to face the enemy king, then check with the rook.

name: Two-rook ladder
lesson: The rooks take turns: one guards a line, the other checks on the next line, walking the king to the edge like a ladder. If the king comes close to a rook, move that rook far away along its line.
tip: Keep the rooks far from the enemy king.

name: King in front of the pawn
lesson: With your king on the sixth rank in front of the pawn, you always win. Use your king to push the enemy king aside, then walk the pawn home. Don't push the pawn too early.

name: The opposition: win
lesson: Kings facing each other with one square between them: whoever does NOT have to move "has the opposition". Black must move first here, so you can take the opposition and escort the pawn. Your pawn on e2 also gives you spare waiting moves.
tip: Keep your king in front of the pawn and face the enemy king whenever you can.

name: The opposition: hold
lesson: The same position, but White moves first, so now you (Black) can hold. Stay in front of the pawn and step straight in front of White's king every time it moves up.
tip: When White's king steps up, face it.

name: Get in front of the pawn
lesson: The defending king belongs directly in front of the pawn. From there you can always take the opposition, and the pawn never gets through.
tip: Block the pawn's path with your king.

name: The square rule
lesson: Draw a square from the pawn to its promotion rank. If your king can step inside that square, it catches the pawn. Here Black just makes it.
tip: Move diagonally towards the promotion square.

name: The outside passed pawn
lesson: An extra pawn far from the kings works as a decoy. Push it; the enemy king has to chase it, and your king eats the pawns on the other side.
tip: Push the a-pawn to drag Black's king away, then go for the kingside.

name: Lucena: build a bridge
lesson: The most important rook ending. Push the enemy king away with a check (Rd1+), put your rook on the 4th rank (Rd4), walk your king out, and when the checks come, block them with your rook. That is "building a bridge".
tip: Rd1+ first, then Rd4, then walk the king out towards your rook.

name: Philidor: third-rank defence
lesson: The key rook-ending defence. Keep your rook on the 6th rank so White's king can't come forward. The moment the pawn advances to e6, swing your rook to the back and check from behind.
tip: Rook stays on the 6th until the pawn goes to e6, then check from behind.

name: The wrong bishop
lesson: A rook pawn plus a bishop that can't control the promotion corner can't win if your king reaches that corner. Stay in the corner and don't leave it.
tip: Shuffle between h8 and g8 or h7.
